name: John Hayhurst

nadir.desc: The property consists of multiple structures with green roofs set within a dense pine forest|A winding river or stream runs along one side of the site with open grassy meadow areas adjacent to the water|Dirt and gravel access roads connect the buildings|Scattered clearings and tree cover dominate the parcel|The developed area is relatively compact within the larger wooded landscape.

alpha.desc: The approach to the property is dominated by dense pine forest|Portions of the river and open meadow are visible through the trees|Access roads wind through the wooded area|The main structures are largely screened by the surrounding tree canopy from this angle.

bravo.desc: The left side of the property shows dense pine forest with the winding river and open grassy areas visible|Portions of the green-roofed structures appear through the trees|Dirt access roads run through the site|The overall setting is heavily wooded with limited open ground near the buildings.

charlie.desc: The rear of the property shows multiple green-roofed structures nestled among dense pine trees|The winding river and adjacent meadow are clearly visible|Dirt and gravel roads provide internal access|Tree cover remains heavy across most of the site, with open areas concentrated near the water.

delta.desc: The right side of the property shows dense pine forest surrounding the green-roofed structures|The river curves along the edge of the site with open meadow nearby|Access roads are visible winding through the trees|The buildings remain partially screened by the surrounding canopy.

considerations: Vehicle access is provided by dirt and gravel roads that wind through dense pine forest to reach the cluster of green-roofed structures. Multiple buildings are present on the site. A winding river or stream runs along one side of the property with open meadow areas adjacent to the water. Heavy tree cover surrounds the developed area and may limit visibility and movement. The property is located in a rural, wooded setting near Sunriver with limited neighboring development visible in the immediate vicinity.
clarifications: Which structure is the primary building or main entrance? Are the dirt and gravel access roads passable for standard emergency vehicles in all seasons? Is there a bridge or designated crossing over the river within or near the property? Do any gates control access from S Century Dr onto the internal roads? How much clear space exists around the main structures given the surrounding dense tree cover?
